widgets_values:
CUPID3D ON A CLEANED PLATE

Reconstructs the subject in 3D and drops it back onto the same photo with the subject painted out, so it can be moved around the scene freely.

NEEDS, BEYOND THIS PACK
- ComfyUI-NKD-Klein-Tools — Klein Pre/Postsampling, Box Detections
- ComfyUI-NKD-Basic-Tools — NKD Loader
- ComfyUI-NKD-VFX-Tools — NKD Preview 3D
- ComfyUI-NKD-Notes — the hints and the guided tour
- comfyui_controlnet_aux — AIO Aux Preprocessor, for the scene depth
- RES4LYF — ClownsharKSampler Beta
Models: birefnet.safetensors for Remove Background, and the "Klein 3 Distilled" bundle inside NKD Loader.

THE FLOW
- Remove Background (BiRefNet) returns a FOREGROUND mask, so it feeds Cupid3D straight in. No InvertMask here, that is only needed for LoadImage's own MASK, which is 1 - alpha.
- The Klein 3 pass reuses that same mask as a "remove" edit: it paints the subject out of the photo and leaves a clean plate.
- The If/Else Switch picks what the viewer sits on, the cleaned plate (true) or the untouched photo (false). Whatever it picks also sets the render size through Get Image Size, so the camera and the plate can never disagree.
- Depth Anything V2 turns that same plate into a depth map, which the viewer's occlude tab uses to tuck the mesh behind things already in the scene.
- camera_info describes the input image exactly as it was fed in, so the plate needs no reframing.

place_on_ground puts the mesh on y=0, resting on the viewer's floor rather than straddling the origin; the camera moves with it. crop_to_content is off in this one, so the pose is solved on the full frame.

Swap the photo for your own and the only thing to revisit is the Klein prompt and the box detections.

properties.text:
# Load Image

Load the image you want to work on.

texts.es:
# Load Image

Carga la imagen sobre la que quieres trabajar.

properties.text:
# Remove Background

BiRefNet gets the mask of the object for you, but you can always swap it for a more manual method.

texts.es:
# Remove Background

BiRefNet obtiene automáticamente la máscara del objeto, pero siempre lo puedes sustituir por otro método más manual.

properties.text:
# Cupid3D Reconstruct

Rebuilds the subject in 3D and, along the way, works out the camera that took the photo.

### `place_on_ground`
Leaves the mesh resting on the viewer's floor instead of straddling the origin, so you can move it around the scene without repositioning it first. The camera moves with it, so the alignment with the photo holds.

### `crop_to_content`
Off here, so the pose is solved on the whole frame. Turn it on when the subject comes out small inside the image.

### `steps` and `cfg_strength`
Both sampling stages use them. If the silhouette comes out wrong, check the mask before raising them: that is almost always where the problem is.

texts.es:
# Cupid3D Reconstruct

Reconstruye el sujeto en 3D y, de paso, calcula la cámara con la que se hizo la foto.

### `place_on_ground`
Deja la malla apoyada en el suelo del visor en vez de atravesada por el origen, para que puedas moverla por la escena sin recolocarla antes. La cámara se mueve con ella, así que la alineación con la foto no se pierde.

### `crop_to_content`
Aquí está apagado, así que la pose se resuelve sobre el fotograma entero. Enciéndelo cuando el sujeto salga pequeño dentro de la imagen.

### `steps` y `cfg_strength`
Valen para las dos etapas del muestreo. Si la silueta sale mal, antes de subirlos revisa la máscara: casi siempre el problema está ahí.

properties.text:
# Klein Box Detections

Tells Klein what is in the image and what to do with it. The action here is **remove**, so it marks the subject to be taken out of the photo.

If your object is complex and the model does not quite get it, describe it in `desc` so the prompt is built in more detail.

texts.es:
# Klein Box Detections

Le dice a Klein qué hay en la imagen y qué hacer con ello. Aquí la acción es **remove**, así que marca al sujeto para que desaparezca de la foto.

Si tu objeto es algo complejo y el modelo no termina de entender, descríbelo en `desc` para que se construya el prompt de forma más detallada.

properties.text:
# Klein Presampling: the removal

The prompt is already set up generically for an object removal, but remember you can fine-tune it for a better result. For example you can add something like `fill the gap with the people behind` if you have an object in front of people and need the model to rebuild them.

If the removal leaves a ghost or eats something it should not have, you can also adjust the mask to expand or blur it.

texts.es:
# Klein Presampling: el borrado

El prompt ya está preparado de forma general para hacer un object removal, pero recuerda que puedes afinarlo para obtener un mejor resultado. Por ejemplo puedes añadir algo como `fill the gap with the people behind` si tienes un objeto delante de personas y necesitas que el modelo las reconstruya.

Si el borrado deja un fantasma o se come algo que no tocaba, también puedes ajustar la máscara para expandirla o desenfocarla.

properties.text:
# Remove Object from Image

Chooses whether the viewer gets the original image or a clean plate with the object removed.

texts.es:
# Remove Object from Image

Decide si quieres importar en el visor la imagen original o un cleanplate con el objeto/sujeto borrado.

properties.text:
# NKD Preview 3D

Press `W`, `E` and `R` for the move, rotate and scale gizmos. Same as Maya.

`Q` toggles between global and local.

With `Alt` you can change the position and rotation of the origin, depending on which gizmo is active. That lets you orient it better for more precise manipulations.

I recommend the icon at the top left, which opens the viewer in a full-screen modal and is far more comfortable to work in.

In the occlude tab you can clip the object by its own depth, or put it behind objects in the scene if you have computed the scene depth beforehand.

texts.es:
# NKD Preview 3D

Usa las teclas `W`, `E` y `R` para activar los gizmos de posición, rotación y escala. Como en Maya.

Con `Q` alternas entre global y local.

Con `Alt` puedes modificar la posición y rotación del origen, según el gizmo que tengas activado. Esto te permite orientarlo mejor para hacer manipulaciones más precisas.

Te recomiendo pulsar el icono de arriba a la izquierda para abrir el visor en un modal a pantalla completa y trabajar de forma más cómoda.

En la pestaña de occlude, puedes recortar el objeto basado en su propia profundidad o colocarlo detrás de objetos de la escena si la has calculado previamente.
